page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The instance delivers 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It includes 480 MB of L3 cache, 256.0 GB of system memory providing 4.0 GB per vCPU, and a bundled 3,780 GB local NVMe SSD. No dedicated GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-threaded performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 86,642.75 falling into the top tier and a stress-ng multi-core result of 67,260.4 in the top quartile. Single-core performance is moderate, registering a stress-ng score of 2,256.48. Hardware support for Intel AMX (int8 and tile) and AVX-512 extensions bolsters specialized vector operations and lightweight machine learning inference, demonstrated by prompt processing throughput of 3,946.15 tokens per second on small models. Memory throughput is solid, delivering 326.02 GB/s in uncached large-block reads.

With integrated NVMe storage and balanced compute-to-memory proportions, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads that require low-latency scratch space without relying solely on network-attached volumes. High throughput in static web serving (104.9 GB/s) and key-value operations (111.2 million Redis SET ops/sec) makes the D64ds_v7 suitable for high-traffic web applications, in-memory caching layers, relational database servers, and distributed data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 64 dedicated vCPUs on 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 256 GB of system memory alongside 3,780 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage. It incorporates 480 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix extensions including Intel AMX and AVX-512. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute with a PassMark CPU score of 86,642.75 and static web serving throughput reaching 104.9 GB/s, coupled with strong Redis throughput of 111.2 million operations per second. While single-core performance remains average, the high core density and integrated high-speed local disk provide balanced resource efficiency for relational databases, distributed caching, batch data processing, and scalable web serving tiers.
